goal: Move the packaged WPF app's persistent settings to an update-stable packaged app store instead of relying on WPF Settings upgrade folders.
must_include: Explains that `Settings.Default.Upgrade()` is looking at WPF user.config version folders and does not reliably bridge the changing Desktop Bridge/MSIX `App.exe_Url_...` hash shown in the fixture.
Recommends persisting packaged-app preferences in `Windows.Storage.ApplicationData.Current.LocalSettings` for the MSIX/Desktop Bridge build.
Copies values between the existing WPF `Properties.Settings.Default` model and `LocalSettings` at startup/save time if the app still needs WPF settings for unpackaged runs.
Calls out that complex values such as collections may need serialization before storing them in `LocalSettings`.
must_not: Claims keeping the assembly version unchanged will make `Settings.Default.Upgrade()` find the previous MSIX settings folder.
Suggests writing into `Program Files` or the package install location for user preferences.
Deletes user data on update as an acceptable migration strategy.
acceptable_alternatives: Create a one-time migration that reads any discoverable legacy WPF settings and then writes future values to `ApplicationData.LocalSettings`.
Use `ApplicationData.LocalFolder` for larger serialized settings files instead of `LocalSettings` key/value storage.
Use a package-aware app data abstraction that selects WPF settings when unpackaged and WinRT application data when packaged.
solved: The answer stops relying on WPF Settings upgrade folders for the packaged app and stores update-surviving preferences in the package's application data.
partial: The answer recommends `ApplicationData.LocalSettings` but does not address copying or serializing existing WPF settings.
notes: The accepted source answer used UWP terminology because Desktop Bridge gives the WPF process package identity and access to WinRT application data APIs.
